title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, point-free framework for 'tame' spaces. A set M of 'pieces' carries primitive relations. These are ≤ (inclusion), ≪ (roughly 'is relatively compact in' / 'interior-contained'), and a separation-type relation, either ≭ or ∥ (disjointness of closures). From these he derives 'supports' (supp, cosupp), boundaries ∂X and interiors X°. The surrounding pages formulate axioms named 'Mag ...', so the structure is probably what he calls a 'magma' or similar.

On this page he proposes changing the primitive vocabulary. Instead of ≭ or ∥ he wants to take as primitive a relation X |∘| Y, heuristically meaning X° ∥ Y° (the interiors are disjoint). The aim is to give a reasonable meaning to the interior X° even when one cannot otherwise prove it is non-empty (he refers to an example at '𝒢 p.53').

He motivates the change with a test case: a simplicial multiplicity, i.e. a simplicial complex (S, M ⊂ 𝔓_f(S)).
- M is presumably a down-closed family of finite subsets containing all singletons {x} (left-margin note).
- He takes ≤ = inclusion of faces, ≪ = ≤, and ≭ always true.
- X ∥ Y is defined by X̃ ∩ Ỹ = ∅, where X̃ is the closed subcomplex of faces of X; this means X and Y are 'non-neighbours', i.e. they share no vertex.
- The lattice of supports of this structure is then Σ_M ≅ 𝔓(S), arbitrary vertex sets, and the support of a simplex X is its own vertex set.

With the 'plausible' definition X° = supp X ∩ cosupp ∂X one gets a degenerate answer. For dim X ≥ 1, ∂X has the same vertex support as X, so its cosupport is the complement of X and X° = X ∩ (S∖X) = ∅. Only for a vertex (∂X = ∅, with X in what he calls L) is X° non-empty. Hence his remark 'C'est triste mais c'est vrai'.

The disjointness relation ∥ alone only sees vertices, so the open simplices are invisible in the derived support calculus. This is why interior-disjointness must be primitive. On the next page he indeed adopts ≤, ≪, |∘| as primitives. He derives a 'non-overlap' relation from |∘|, and states axiom Mag 4'': distinct faces of a common simplex are |∘|-related. This is exactly the statement that distinct open simplices are disjoint.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The computation X° = ∅ for positive-dimensional simplices is correct for the stated definitions.
Σ_M ≅ 𝔓(S) tacitly needs every vertex {x} to lie in M (and M to be closed under taking faces); the margin note seems to add exactly this hypothesis.
'X ∈ L' is unexplained on this page; it should presumably mean 'X is a vertex / minimal element (∂X = ∅)'.

ideas.what: Taking 'interiors disjoint' (|∘|) as a primitive relation of a point-free topological structure, instead of disjointness of closures or 'non-overlap'
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology / Region Connection Calculus (the 'discrete' / non-overlap relation DR vs. disconnection DC); Whitehead–de Laguna point-free geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna (1922), B. Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 calls for an axiomatic tame topology but has no such primitive relations

ideas.what: Test case: simplicial complex as an ordered set with ≪ = ≤ and ∥ = 'no common vertex'; the support lattice is 𝔓(S) and naive interiors vanish except at vertices
ideas.modern_name: Failure of a vertex-based (discrete) locale to see open cells; the correct 'point' set is the face poset with its Alexandrov topology (McCord), where open simplices are points

ideas.what: Defining interior as X° = supp X ∩ cosupp ∂X
ideas.modern_name: Interior as complement of boundary in a lattice of supports (closure algebra style)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics for analysis situs independently converge on the primitive relations of mereotopology / qualitative spatial reasoning: inclusion, interior-disjointness and closure-disjointness. The simplicial example shows why the non-overlap relation cannot be derived from closure-disjointness at the level of supports. This link between Grothendieck's tame-topology programme and the region-based topology literature (Clarke, RCC) seems not to have been made.
missed.quote: J'ai envie de prendre ... comme relations primitives, en plus de ≤ et de ≪, et au lieu de ≭ ou de ∥, la relation X |∘| Y ⟺ X° ∥ Y°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It might interest historians of the 'tame topology' programme and people working on point-free / region-based topology. However, the mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: An interesting design decision in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic topology, with an illustrative but elementary simplicial computation. The idea of primitive overlap-type relations is well known in mereotopology, so only the historical link is new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the quoted word is probably 'magma' or 'magasin' rather than 'ensemble', consistent with the 'Mag' axioms on the next page.
'on sait pas forcément prouver' is probably 'on ne sait pas forcément prouver qu'il serait vide'.
The left-margin note likely reads roughly 'M partie saturée de 𝔓_f(S) pour ⊂, contenant les {x}', i.e. a down-closed family of faces containing all singletons.
In the struck-through middle passage, the surviving fragment seems to be '... si on a ... cosupp(X)^∂ = ∅' (uncertain).
